runs.name: Versigent PLC; NYSE VGNT, SEC CIK 0002078008, a Jersey company with its principal office in Schaffhausen, Switzerland; low-voltage and high-voltage vehicle electrical architectures (wire harnesses: signal, power and data distribution) sold mainly to light and commercial vehicle OEMs; Aptiv PLC's former Electrical Distribution Systems segment, spun off 2026-04-01 at one share for every three Aptiv shares; formerly Cyprium Holdings Ltd and Versigent Ltd; no 10-K filed yet
runs.entry: The v5 re-run order, unattended work-hours cycle, one dispatched analyst under the canonical brief, from scratch. The brief's departures: the repository path after the move of 2026-10-25; the lines of evidence derived by the analyst; and, with no 10-K on file, the Form 10 information statement (Exhibit 99.1 to the 10-12B/A of 2026-03-06, accession 0001193125-26-096776) standing in for Items 1, 1A and 7, with the two 10-Qs and Aptiv PLC's 10-Ks for the segment's history. Price **$41.40** (close 2026-10-23, aggregator, flagged) x **70,835,265 shares** (10-Q cover at 2026-07-31, accession 0002078008-26-000018; cover_shares.py agrees) = cap **$2,932.6M**; sovereign **5.33%** (Treasury 30-year par, 2026-10-23). The span that could be read for the business itself is FY2023 to FY2025 and the first half of 2026: before 2023 the harness business sat inside Aptiv's Signal and Power Solutions and Delphi's segments together with connectors. **Q1 IN** (a hand-assembled wire-harness maker selling on contracts that last a model's life; the deciding variables, price terms, labour and copper pass-through, stated in the filing; wiring content per vehicle under electrification and zone architectures the one doubt, carried to Q2). **Q2 OUT** on the filing's own words: customer contracts "require step-downs in component pricing" of "typically 1% to 3% per year", customers may terminate for convenience to obtain price reductions, competition "based primarily on price", an industry that "historically has had excess capacity", new entrants from China named, 138,000 people of whom 129,000 hourly in low-cost labour countries, restructuring every year ($48M, $101M, $86M), and Pricing -$18M in Q2 2026 after the spin (10-Q MD&A, found after the verdict). Peers: Lear the only named rival that files with the SEC; its E-Systems segment margin 12.6% to 14.1% in 2014 to 2018, 1.4% to 4.1% in 2020 to 2025, about 5% to 6% pre-tax on segment assets; Versigent's GAAP operating margin 6.6%, 5.5%, 6.1% (adjusted 6.9% to 7.6%) in FY2023 to FY2025; Yazaki, Sumitomo Electric and Furukawa Electric flagged as not SEC filers. Contrary evidence written down by the analyst: about 36% and 42% pre-tax on the operating capital the business needs (supplier credit funds the working capital, capital spending below depreciation), a margin above Lear's in all three years, long incumbency and new awards. Q3 to Q12 not reached; facts after the stop not weighed: equity $1,848M to $284M because a $1,894M dividend was paid to Aptiv out of $2,063M of new borrowing; net debt $1,670M at 2026-06-30; pension obligations $214M; five customers 65% of sales; Adjusted Operating Income and Adjusted EBITDA featured; a $250M buyback authorized with no stated price; no integrity fact found; no proxy filed. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash (operating cash flow less all capital spending, stock pay and the minority share) -$118M, $447M, $430M in FY2023 to FY2025; three-year window a CONVENTION of the run; FY2023 aberrational by the filer's own words (UAW strikes, chip shortage), shown both ways as a CONVENTION of the run; sales flat, so the no-growth case alone; range **$43.43 to $92.57 a share all-equity (central)**, depreciation variant $41.32 to $84.22, equity-only $34.97 to $84.10; no case earns the floor at the price (5.50% and 9.53% on enterprise value); fair price **$25.23 all-equity**, $31.73 equity-only. Framework gaps for the operator: no rule for a spin-off with fewer than five filed years (build from the parent's combined segment, shorten the window, or TOO HARD (WORK)); how much one SEC-filing rival's cycle may carry in Q2's section C when the other named rivals do not file; whether 9.5% is "about ten percent" at the floor; the commit-after-each-question line for a file that closes at Q2. Could not get: any separate filed history before FY2023, a 10-K or proxy, the earnings press releases (guidance not checked), the non-SEC rivals' costs, the cause of FY2023's $384M current tax charge. Analyst's commits: four pathspec commits of its own paths, last `0eaf2aa9`. Dispatcher's check: check_framework PASS; 61 id citations resolve, no E-ids, no citation slip, 29 adjacent fragment pairs checked, four checker mispairings resolved by hand (`dispatcher_cite_check2.py`); no tracked research file over 200 KB. Contamination declared: a `Test Runs/` listing showing fourteen other runs' file names dated 2026-10-26, session-start commit subjects of the UTL run, a memory index line naming no company; none used. Position note filled at the fold: not held. Not armed: the box is not OUT at Q7 or IN.
runs.narr: OUT at Q2: a hand-assembled wire-harness maker whose customers take 1% to 3% a year off the price by contract and may terminate for convenience, in an industry the filing says competes primarily on price with historic excess capacity; the one rival on the SEC record, Lear E-Systems, fell from 12% to 14% margins to 1% to 4% over the cycle. Computation only: all-equity range $43.43 to $92.57 on three filed years vs $41.40, no case earns the floor, fair $25.23 all-equity.
